findings.title: Bounded refuge against compelled inclination
findings.claim: Within the Joseph-in-prison pericope, the named prison can be heard as a bounded refuge against a summons that would draw him toward the women's demand and into the knowledge-deficient conduct named at the end.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies prison, summons, inclination, and the final class of the ignorant. The preceding command and threat, together with the supplied protective-hold occurrence, make the comparison a choice of boundary, so confinement changes from an imposed loss of movement into a chosen protection of agency.
findings.reader_payoff: The comparison acquires a spatial and moral geometry: a closed place can preserve freedom of response when the open field of access is coercive.
findings.containment: The plain preference for prison and the conditional fear of yielding remain intact. This does not claim that confinement is intrinsically good or that the summons verb lexically means coercion.

epistemic.reason: A trusted channel nomination supplies the relation and exact focus branches; the protective-hold branch is a bounded nominated context image, so the finding is retained with its source boundary explicit.

findings.title: Protection as renewed cooperation
findings.claim: Protection is presented as renewed cooperation: prior redirection, human self-holding, petition, and answered turning form a sequence in which moral safety is repeatedly received and enacted rather than possessed once.
findings.mechanism: The supplied redirection appears before and after the focus, self-holding appears in 12:32, and an answering response follows in 12:34. The repeated operation meets the focus petition and changes protection from a stored status into an ongoing relation between divine turning and human restraint.
findings.reader_payoff: Resistance and prayer belong to one continuing exchange: earlier protection can be remembered without making renewed protection unnecessary.
findings.containment: The focus remains a direct request and conditional warning. The broader claim about recurrent cooperation is attributed inference; the alternative that the repetitions narrate one continuous rescue remains live.

epistemic.reason: The exact 12:24, 12:32, focus, and 12:34 coordinates land on the supplied redirection and holding relations, while their sequence is legacy-attributed contextual evidence.

findings.title: Personal plea within universal lordship
findings.claim: The personal vocative Rabbim meets Fatiha's Rabb of the worlds, so the request for protection can be heard as directed to the same governing Lord whose care extends beyond this immediate household.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus and external Arabic establish a local Rabb contact, while the broadened universal scope is a bounded overlay inference with no separate candidate or support record.
